articles.title: FSS Union Blames Policy-Bound Oversight for Leveraged ETF Losses - Seoul Economic Daily
articles.summary: FSS Union Blames Policy-Bound Oversight for Leveraged ETF Losses  Seoul Economic Daily
articles.full_text:
The labor union of South Korea's Financial Supervisory Service has blamed investor losses tied to the introduction of single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds on a supervisory system it says is subordinate to policy. The union argues the FSS lacks the authority to check decisions made by policy authorities while still bearing responsibility for supervision after the fact.
The union said so in a statement released on the 21st titled "The Culprit Is a Financial Supervisory System Subordinate to Policy." "Even when financial policies pushed by the administration carry side effects and problems, there are structural limits that make it hard to voice independent views, out of concern over institutional disadvantages such as budget allocations," the union said.
The union took issue with the current structure in which the Financial Services Commission directs and supervises the FSS while approving its staffing quota and budget. Because the FSS has no authority to enact or amend supervisory regulations or to place items on the FSC's agenda, it cannot fix rules itself even when it detects risks early, the union said. The FSS governor can request that an item be tabled at the FSC, but the power to do so rests with the commission. The union stressed that the backdrop to the launch of the product lies in "the current financial supervisory system, which has been changed for the worse so that it cannot help but be subordinate to policy."
Under these conditions, the union said, when consumer losses occur the FSS is held responsible for supervisory failures after the fact, and the administration's control grows stronger through discussions over designating the FSS as a public institution or through conditions attached to deferring such a designation — a vicious cycle that keeps repeating. It cited the 2011 savings bank insolvency crisis, the 2013 Tong Yang Group commercial paper debacle and the 2020 private fund scandal as cases that exposed the limits of the supervisory system.
To secure the independence of the supervisory body, the union demanded that the FSC's authority to direct and supervise the FSS and to approve its budget be transferred to the National Assembly, and that a parliamentary confirmation hearing be introduced for the appointment of the FSS governor. It also argued that the FSS should be given the power to enact and amend supervisory regulations and to table items at the FSC, so that it can institutionally present views that differ from those of policy authorities. The union further urged a revision of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions to exclude the FSS from designation as a public institution.

articles.title: Gold slips as investors await Fed rate signals - The Economic Times
articles.summary: Gold slips as investors await Fed rate signals  The Economic Times
articles.full_text:
Synopsis
Gold prices fell slightly as investors monitored the Federal Reserve's major interest rate decision. The anticipated meeting will provide key insights into future economic policies. Economists expect the Fed to hold rates steady, emphasizing inflation concerns. The Bank of Japan is also projected to raise interest rates in December. Other precious metals, including silver and platinum, experienced minimal changes during this period.
Fundamentals
Spot gold was down 0.1% at $4,118.64 per ounce by 0018 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery dropped 0.1% to $4,137.60.
The Fed will skip raising interest rates this month and deliver a hike in December, according to nearly all economists polled by Reuters, as policymakers signal patience even as stubborn inflation argues for a tougher response.
Focus has turned to the Fed's October 27-28 policy meeting and next week's Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) data, a key gauge closely watched by the central bank as it targets a 2% inflation rate.
According to CME's FedWatch Tool, traders are pricing in an 84% chance that the central bank will leave rates unchanged next week, while expectations for a hike in December remain at 90%.
Higher interest rates typically weigh on gold prices because they increase the opportunity cost of holding bullion, which does not pay interest.
The Bank of Japan will raise rates in December to 1.50%, following June and September increases, according to a majority of economists in a Reuters poll, keeping up a quicker pace in a campaign that started with just one rate rise a year.
Bank of England policymaker Megan Greene said the risks of a pickup in broader inflation from the energy price shock caused by the Iran war were greater than the BoE expected. She reiterated her view that interest rates should go up.
On the geopolitical front, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian discussed mediation efforts and regional developments during a meeting with Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, in Tehran, Iran's Nournews reported on Tuesday.
Among other metals, spot silver steadied at $57.95 per ounce, platinum rose 0.5% to $1,656.10 and palladium was little changed at $1,102.13.

articles.full_text:
Key takeaways
- Bitcoin faces another $80,000 test before October's Fed decision
- US spot Bitcoin ETFs attract $526.7 million in inflows
- Economists expect a Fed pause despite persistent inflation
Bitcoin could revisit $80,000 ahead of the Federal Reserve's October 28 interest-rate decision, even after a rebound toward $83,000 and a sharp recovery in institutional ETF demand.
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds attracted $526.7 million on October 19, according to Farside Investors, reversing an $82.4 million withdrawal recorded during the previous session. BlackRock's IBIT led with $665.2 million in inflows, partially offset by withdrawals from Fidelity and Grayscale.
The recovery followed Bitcoin's October 19 climb to approximately $82,830, a five-day high. However, the cryptocurrency remains below its early-October peak near $87,300, leaving investors focused on whether improving institutional demand can withstand another potentially restrictive Fed announcement.
Bitcoin ETF Inflows Rebound $526.7 Million Before Fed Decision
The ETF recovery represents a significant shift following several weeks of uneven institutional buying.
Between October 5 and 9, Bitcoin funds recorded approximately $679 million in weekly outflows. Withdrawals subsequently reached $729 million across October 7–8 alone, with BlackRock and Fidelity among the leading contributors.
The latest $526.7 million inflow offsets a substantial portion of that selling, but one positive session does not establish a sustained demand recovery.
Bitcoin's earlier October decline also coincided with rising Treasury yields, a stronger dollar and a broader reduction in risk exposure.
More recently, a liquidation wave pushed Bitcoin below $82,000, demonstrating how leveraged positions can amplify relatively modest price movements.
Fed Expected to Hold Rates as December Hike Looms
The Federal Reserve will announce its next policy decision on October 28, following a two-day meeting.
A Reuters survey of 100 economists published October 20 found that 94 expect rates to remain unchanged at 3.75%-4.00%. However, economists surveyed anticipate another quarter-point increase in December.
Persistent inflation explains the uncertainty.
US consumer prices rose 3.7% annually in September, up from 3.4% in August. Meanwhile, the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield has climbed above 5%, increasing the appeal of interest-bearing assets relative to speculative investments.
Bitcoin benefited when expectations of an immediate hike diminished, but its latest rebound has not eliminated the macroeconomic pressures that drove previous declines.
Even if policymakers leave rates unchanged, commentary suggesting additional tightening in December could influence bond yields and cryptocurrency valuations.
Bitcoin Price Prediction: $80K Support or $85K Recovery?
Bitcoin's short-term outlook depends on whether buyers can maintain support around $80,000–$82,000.
QCP Capital previously identified that region as a potential buying zone, while October's decline briefly pushed BTC below $80,000 before buyers returned.
A renewed move below $82,000 would expose the $80,000 psychological level. If that support fails, the $78,500–$80,000 region becomes a possible downside scenario rather than a confirmed target.
Alternatively, reclaiming $83,000 could open another test of $84,400–$85,000. Sustained buying above that region would strengthen the case for an eventual return toward October's $87,300 high.
An earlier short-term forecast also identified the $80,000 area as important, although its modeled probabilities are not reliable indicators of what will happen after the Fed announcement.

articles.title: Mashujaa Day 2026: Ruto’s Ksh4.2T market claim faces fresh test as inflation hits 6.8% - People Daily
articles.summary: Mashujaa Day 2026: Ruto’s Ksh4.2T market claim faces fresh test as inflation hits 6.8%  People Daily
articles.full_text:
President William Ruto has defended his economic record by pointing to rising stock market valuations, increased foreign investment and agricultural reforms, but the latest official statistics reveal a more complicated picture of Kenya’s recovery.
Speaking on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, during Mashujaa Day celebrations in Eldoret, Ruto said the value of Kenya’s stock market had doubled from Ksh2 trillion in 2022 to Ksh4.2 trillion, while foreign direct investment had more than doubled over three years.
“Over the last four years, we have grown our economy, stabilised our exchange rates, brought inflation under control, expanded access to credit, and reformed our capital markets,” the President said.
However, Kenya’s latest inflation data, agricultural production figures and economic growth statistics show that some of the gains require qualification.
According to the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS), annual inflation rose to 6.8 per cent in September 2026, driven partly by increases in food and transport costs. Food and non-alcoholic beverage prices rose by 9.5 per cent, while transport costs increased by 15.6 per cent over the year.
The figures complicate the government’s claim that inflation has been brought under control, particularly for households and businesses facing higher operating expenses.
Market gains, investment questions
Ruto said Kenya’s stock market valuation had increased to Ksh4.2 trillion, presenting the expansion as evidence of stronger investor confidence.
The latest KNBS leading economic indicators dashboard available in July placed market capitalisation at approximately Ksh3.99 trillion. That is a substantial valuation, although it does not independently confirm the Ksh4.2 trillion figure cited by the President.
A rising stock market can help listed companies raise capital and increase the value of investors’ holdings. However, market capitalisation reflects share prices and the number of shares outstanding; it is not equivalent to new investment flowing into businesses.
Foreign direct investment provides another measure of investor interest.
Ruto said annual FDI had increased from Ksh194 billion in 2022 to Ksh413 billion in 2025. The figures are consistent with reported data from the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), which put Kenya’s FDI inflows at Ksh413 billion in 2025, compared with Ksh297 billion in 2024 and Ksh194 billion in 2022
The increase is a positive signal for Kenya’s investment prospects. Nevertheless, the value of inflows alone does not establish how much new employment was created, how investment was distributed across sectors or how much capital went into productive capacity.
On economic growth, KNBS reported that Kenya’s GDP expanded by 4.6 per cent in 2025, down slightly from 4.7 per cent in 2024. The economy subsequently grew by 5.1 per cent year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, indicating an acceleration in activity.
The International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) October outlook also projects global growth of 3.1 per cent in 2026, with risks including geopolitical tensions, renewed trade disputes and fiscal vulnerabilities.
Those pressures could affect export demand, financing conditions and investment decisions in emerging economies.
Maize figures disputed
Agriculture was central to Ruto’s defence of the administration’s economic performance. He said fertiliser subsidies and reforms had lowered production costs, improved farmer earnings and increased domestic food production.
“Today, it costs 2,000 shillings under our subsidy programme,” he said, referring to the price of a bag of fertiliser.
The President also said maize production had risen from 34.3 million bags in 2022 to 71 million bags in 2025.
However, KNBS’s 2026 Economic Survey puts maize production at 34.2 million bags in 2022 and 45.8 million bags in 2025. The official figures therefore do not support the 71 million bags cited in the speech.
The discrepancy is material because maize output affects food availability, import requirements and prices paid by households and food processors.
KNBS data show that agricultural performance in 2025 was mixed. The sector grew by 2.8 per cent, while maize production increased by 2.2 per cent. Tea production declined by 7.8 per cent, sugarcane output fell by 24.7 per cent, and coffee production rose by 3.8 per cent. Milk production increased by 3.5 per cent to 5.52 billion litres.
These figures suggest that agricultural reforms have coincided with improvements in some commodities, but the results have not been uniform across the sector.
For farmers and agribusinesses, lower input costs and better farm-gate prices can improve margins. Yet higher production costs elsewhere, weather conditions and market prices also determine whether those gains translate into stronger earnings.
Credit and business test
Ruto said more than 10 million Kenyans regularly borrowed through the Hustler Fund and that Ksh98 billion had been advanced without collateral. He also announced plans to inject another Ksh5 billion into the programme before the end of 2026.
“Credit to the private sector has expanded,” he said, arguing that improved access to financing was supporting businesses.
The announcement comes as policymakers seek to expand lending to small enterprises, which often struggle to obtain affordable credit.
However, borrower numbers and cumulative disbursements do not establish how many businesses have grown, created jobs or remained profitable. Repayment rates, repeat borrowing and business survival are important measures of the fund’s effectiveness.
Ruto also highlighted Kenya’s trade agreements with the European Union and United Arab Emirates, as well as efforts to expand exports to China and maintain access to the United States market.
The agreements could create opportunities for exporters, but the benefits depend on market demand, product standards, logistics costs and the ability of Kenyan firms to compete internationally.
Ultimately, the President’s economic scorecard contains measurable gains, particularly in foreign investment and recent economic growth.
But rising inflation, uneven agricultural performance and discrepancies in some headline figures show why official statistics matter.
For businesses and households, the decisive test will be whether these gains translate into lower operating costs, affordable food, sustainable jobs and stronger purchasing power.

articles.summary: EAAA India Alternatives Fixes Price Band at ₹1,585 to ₹1,665 per Share for ₹1,200 Crore IPO  EquityBulls
articles.full_text:
In continuation of its earlier disclosure regarding the Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) filing, Edelweiss Financial Services Limited (NSE: EDELWEISS, BSE: 532922) has announced that its subsidiary, EAAA India Alternatives Limited, has fixed the price band and bid lot size for its upcoming Initial Public Offering (IPO).
The price band was determined and approved by the IPO Committee of the Board of Directors of EAAA India Alternatives Limited at its meeting held today, October 20, 2026. The regulatory intimation was submitted to BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited pursuant to the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.
Price Band and Bid Lot Structure
The parameters for the public issue of equity shares of face value ₹5 each are structured as follows:
- Floor Price: ₹1,585 per equity share
- Cap Price: ₹1,665 per equity share
- Minimum Bid Lot: 9 equity shares (and in multiples of 9 equity shares thereafter)

articles.title: Downside Pressure Deepens on PMET Resources Inc. Amid Broad Lithium Correction Risks and Cautious Near-Term Sentiment - kalkine.ca
articles.summary: Downside Pressure Deepens on PMET Resources Inc. Amid Broad Lithium Correction Risks and Cautious Near-Term Sentiment  kalkine.ca
articles.full_text:
Key Highlights:
- Persistent Downside Pressure: PMET shares experienced a notable session decline, closing down by 3.04% on October 19, 2026, driven by broad-based selling pressure and a cautious investor backdrop.
- Valuation Concerns: Elevated valuation dynamics relative to near-term cash generation leave the equity vulnerable to negative re-rating risks.
- Sector Headwinds: Sluggish pricing environments across critical battery minerals and broader commodity volatility continue to depress sentiment toward early-stage development assets.
- Financing and Capital Intensity: Substantial ongoing capital requirements for advanced-stage exploration and project advancement heighten market sensitivity to dilution and funding conditions.
Introduction
PMET Resources Inc.
(TSX:PMET) operates as a critical mineral exploration and development enterprise focused primarily on advancing its district-scale, wholly-owned Shaakichiuwaanaan property (formerly known as Corvette) located in the Eeyou Istchee James Bay region of Québec, Canada.
The company’s core business model centers on delineating and developing large-scale pegmatite-hosted lithium resources to supply the rapidly evolving North American electric vehicle and energy storage supply chain.
Principal operational activities are concentrated in northwestern Québec, an established yet logistically challenging mining jurisdiction.
Recently, the company’s shares have faced intensifying downward pressure, closing the session in the red with a 3.
04% pullback on October 19, 2026.
This retreat reflects a confluence of company-specific execution hurdles, waning risk appetite across the junior mining complex, and macro-level uncertainties.
Broader sector conditions remain burdened by persistent softness in lithium spot markets, which has sapped speculative momentum and driven institutional capital outflows from pre-revenue developers.
Furthermore, macroeconomic headwinds, including tighter financing conditions and volatile capital markets, continue to weigh heavily on early-stage resource equities.
As market participants demand tangible cash-flow visibility and lower execution risk, the current operating environment is likely to remain challenging for equities heavily reliant on future capital deployment.

Key Reasons Behind Decline
The recent correction in PMET Resources Inc. shares is rooted in a combination of negative investor sentiment, sector-wide weakness, and growing macroeconomic caution. Investor sentiment toward the lithium exploration sector has turned markedly defensive as market participants re-evaluate the near-term demand trajectory for electric vehicle battery raw materials. This shift has triggered noticeable institutional outflows and speculative selling across pre-production mining names, putting direct downward pressure on share prices. Compounding these sentiment-driven dynamics are growing concerns regarding declining earnings visibility and the capital-intensive nature of advancing large-scale mineral assets from study phases toward eventual construction. With broader commodity markets experiencing heightened volatility, investors have displayed a distinct aversion to assets requiring substantial near-term capital outlays without immediate commercial production horizons. Additionally, broader economic uncertainties, including shifting interest-rate expectations and persistent global growth concerns, have restricted risk capital availability for the junior mining sector, amplifying downward momentum during negative trading sessions.
Risks to Consider
Investors evaluating PMET Resources Inc. must navigate a complex array of structural and operational risks that could influence future share-price performance. Primary among these is funding risk; the substantial capital required to complete ongoing exploration, environmental assessments, and engineering studies exposes the company to potential equity dilution or unfavorable financing terms if market conditions remain subdued. Operational execution issues, including potential project delays, permitting hurdles, or unexpected cost inflation related to remote northern infrastructure development, represent additional threats to shareholder value. Furthermore, ongoing commodity price volatility in the global lithium market directly impacts the perceived economic viability of large-scale development projects, potentially altering long-term cash generation projections. Macroeconomic factors such as persistent interest-rate sensitivity and broader industrial demand slowdowns could further impair liquidity and dampen investor appetite, limiting the company's strategic flexibility in navigating capital markets.
Valuation Perspective
Assessing the valuation of PMET Resources Inc. requires a careful distinction between the company's undeniable long-term fundamental resource potential and its near-term valuation vulnerabilities. While the district-scale nature of the Shaakichiuwaanaan project offers significant strategic allure within the domestic battery supply chain, current market pricing appears demanding when weighed against the absence of near-term operating cash flows. Investor skepticism has grown around capital intensity and the extended timeline required to bring greenfield mineral projects into commercial production. Consequently, downside re-rating risk remains present, as current market expectations leave little margin for operational missteps or extended project timelines. The prevailing valuation profile suggests that future share-price appreciation will require flawless execution, sustained proof of resource expansion, and a broader rehabilitation of investor confidence in the battery metals sector.
Outlook
The forward-looking assessment for PMET Resources Inc. remains cautious and balanced, reflecting a tug-of-war between long-term strategic positioning and near-term macroeconomic headwinds. While the structural shift toward domestic critical mineral supply chains provides a supportive long-term backdrop, near-term operational risks, sector headwinds, and funding requirements dictate a prudent stance. For investor sentiment to sustainably improve, market participants will likely need to see concrete catalysts, including successful navigation of environmental permitting milestones, clearer visibility on capital funding structures, sustained optimization of engineering studies, and a broader stabilization in lithium commodity pricing trends. Until these fundamental milestones are decisively achieved, the equity is likely to remain sensitive to broader market volatility and shifting risk sentiment.

articles.title: Citi: If Oil Prices Don't Fall Back, the Top for 10-Year Treasury Yields May Still Be Ahead - BigGo Finance
articles.summary: Citi: If Oil Prices Don't Fall Back, the Top for 10-Year Treasury Yields May Still Be Ahead  BigGo Finance
articles.full_text:
Whether the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield has finally peaked is the hardest question in global asset allocation today. Citi's latest quantitative cross-asset research leans conservative: until international oil prices clearly retreat, the ultimate peak in Treasury yields may not have truly arrived.
The report, authored by Citi quantitative global macro strategy analysts Alex Saunders and Vinh Vo, reaffirms the team's existing cross-asset analytical framework and adds three new rate-selloff episodes exceeding 70 basis points on top of the original base, without loosening its core conclusion. The report states directly that front-end breakeven inflation rates and a pullback in oil prices are historically the two most reliable leading signals for calling a peak in the 10-year Treasury yield, with an oil price peak being an almost necessary precondition for a yield peak.
In other words, the top in the bond market is not determined solely by the Federal Reserve's rate path—it is tightly tethered to crude oil prices. This logic breaks with the traditional approach of watching only policy rates, and makes current geopolitical risk the most critical variable for the bond market.
Contradictory Signals Make Direction Hard to Call
According to Citi's historical backtesting, clear leading and lagging patterns in cross-asset performance emerge before the 10-year Treasury yield tops out. Among leading indicators, front-end breakeven inflation rates typically roll over one to two months before the peak; flattening of the 5-year to 30-year Treasury curve (5s30s) emerges about a month before the peak; quality stocks perform strongly within a 200-day window around the peak, while growth stocks tend to peak early before the top arrives and then persistently underperform the broader market.
Lagging or non-signals are equally clear. Two-year real rates continue to rise after the yield peak rather than reversing at the turning point; both core and headline consumer price index (CPI) year-over-year readings are lagging indicators, and recent hot CPI prints are not enough to rule out that yields have already peaked; the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) has almost no value in timing a yield turning point, but historically tends to decline after a peak is confirmed.
The problem is that when current market conditions are compared against historical patterns, the signals conflict sharply. On one hand, cyclical stocks have underperformed defensive stocks for two to three consecutive months, and high-yield bond spreads have widened in tandem—characteristics consistent with a post-peak market. On the other hand, breakeven inflation rates are rising rather than falling, the key "pullback" signal has yet to form, the US Dollar Index (DXY) has recently resumed its ascent, and oil prices continue to oscillate at high levels amid geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East and elsewhere. All three indicators point to a yield peak that may still lie ahead.
The report also acknowledges that the 5s30s curve flattening trend has reversed over the past 25 trading days, muddying this previously effective signal and further complicating directional judgment.
Midterm Elections a Variable for Oil Prices
Citi believes the difficulty in timing an oil price peak stems from geopolitical uncertainty that continues to support crude prices. If geopolitical conditions improve—especially after the U.S. midterm elections—the probability of an oil price peak would rise significantly, in turn creating the key condition for a sustained decline in Treasury yields. Until then, near-term yield moves will remain highly uncertain.
Given the conflicting bullish and bearish signals, Citi's cycle model has switched to a "late-cycle" defensive posture. On asset allocation, the model is underweight equities and credit, overweight bonds (excluding Treasuries) and commodities, and has recently cut its equity position further to underweight. The global macro strategy team remains broadly neutral on duration, favors receiving the European Central Bank-versus-Federal Reserve rate spread in rates strategy, and prefers equity exposure over credit.
| Citi Cycle Model Allocation | Position | 
|---|---|
| Equities | Underweight (further cut recently) | 
| Credit | Underweight | 
| Bonds (excluding Treasuries) | Overweight | 
| Commodities | Overweight | 
| Duration | Neutral | 
Note: Citi's cycle model has switched to a "late-cycle" defensive posture; the above reflects the allocation direction disclosed in the report.
The core of this allocation logic is clear: before peak-yield signals become clear and before oil prices and breakeven inflation rates show a decisive pullback, maintaining a neutral, wait-and-see stance on Treasuries—rather than actively going long—is the more prudent position in an environment of normalized geopolitical risk.
Implications for Markets
For bond investors, this report effectively pushes back the timing of "buying the dip." If oil prices stay elevated, inflation expectations will be hard to shake, limiting the downside room for long-dated Treasury yields, and trades betting on a peak-and-reversal in yields may have to wait longer.
For equities, the signals are similarly mixed. Widening high-yield spreads and weakening cyclical stocks typically suggest the market has already priced in a yield peak; but a stronger dollar and rising inflation expectations weigh on growth stock valuations. Citi's choice to prioritize equities over credit reflects greater concern about credit market risk than about the stock market.
Notably, the research identifies the U.S. midterm elections as a potential turning point for oil prices. If the geopolitical climate eases after the vote and oil prices retreat accordingly, that would be the first domino in confirming a peak in Treasury yields; conversely, if oil prices continue to hover at high levels, forecasts for a yield peak will only be pushed back again and again.

articles.title: Euro Forecast: ECB Rate Upgrade Tests EUR/USD Recovery - Exchange Rates UK
articles.summary: Euro Forecast: ECB Rate Upgrade Tests EUR/USD Recovery  Exchange Rates UK
articles.full_text:
The Euro-Dollar Rate Edges Higher as Crédit Agricole Raises Its ECB Rate Forecast
The Euro is recovering against the US Dollar, but Crédit Agricole's higher ECB rate forecast still leaves it cautious about market tightening bets.
The Euro-to-Dollar exchange rate recovered to $1.1230 on Tuesday morning, up 0.15% from Monday's close.
Crédit Agricole has raised its forecast for the European Central Bank's peak deposit rate to 3% in March 2027, adding another increase to its previous outlook.
Yet its new forecast remains below the eventual peak markets were pricing when the bank made the revision.
UBS separately expects EUR/USD to recover to $1.16 by end-2026 and $1.20 by June 2027, provided European risks become less damaging than investors fear.
The latest French unrest is an immediate test of that confidence.
More ECB tightening, but less than markets expect
Crédit Agricole's Louis Harreau expects quarter-point increases in December and March, with an October rise still possible but unlikely.
Higher oil and gas prices have pushed the bank's inflation forecasts upwards, leaving underlying price growth uncomfortably high through next year.
Harreau writes: "In our view, our new inflation forecasts warrant deposit rate hikes until 3.0%. But as things stand currently, we see no reason for the ECB to hike to 3.25%."
"Of course, if gas prices continue increasing, then our core inflation forecasts would change and accordingly our ECB scenario."
The bank expects core inflation to peak in the first quarter of 2027 before easing, weakening the case for extending the hiking cycle beyond March.
Harreau writes: "Until March 2027, we are more or less aligned with the current market pricing (as we have upwardly revised our call and the market has de-priced some hawkishness)."
"Beyond March 2027, markets expect one more hike-by around July 2027. Again, we see this pricing as too high, but 3.25% is still within the limits of what is possible."
Harreau also identifies a larger disagreement further ahead, with markets not pricing the eventual cuts Crédit Agricole expects as inflation declines.
An upward revision to one bank's forecast therefore need not lift the Euro if investors are already assuming a stronger tightening cycle.
The ECB itself remains cautious about how widely expensive energy is spreading through the economy.
In her latest statement to the IMF's policy committee, Christine Lagarde said wage growth had shown no material response to the energy shock and that underlying inflation measures remained broadly stable in September.
She also noted that financing conditions had tightened as long-term interest rates rose.
French bond stress complicates the recovery
That tightening can occur without another ECB decision.
Investors demanding a higher premium to lend to France can also raise funding costs for private borrowers, restraining activity and reducing the amount of additional monetary tightening required.
Crédit Agricole warns that either a sovereign crisis or the fiscal retrenchment needed to repair France's finances would hurt growth.
On Monday, French bonds sold off following weekend riots, with MarketWatch reporting that the 10-year yield rose nearly six basis points to 4.845% early in trading as investors questioned the government's ability to reduce its deficit.
UBS's recovery forecast, published before that unrest, depends partly on a budget agreement restoring confidence.
Its strategists Constantin Bolz and Clémence Dumoncel write: "Although the fiscal situation in France remains challenging and is unlikely to improve materially in the near term, we do not expect a broader European debt crisis."
"Instead, we believe some form of budget agreement is likely to be passed, potentially through the use of Article 49.3."
The bank expects an agreement to narrow France's borrowing premium over Germany and help the Euro recover.
A budget agreement could give the recovery more lasting support than the oversold conditions Scotiabank identified near $1.11.
UBS's longer-term currency forecast also relies on relief from Europe's energy bill.
The UBS strategists write: "With the situation in the Middle East unresolved and the Northern Hemisphere entering the winter season, it is difficult to envisage a significant near-term decline in energy prices. However, in our base case, we expect energy prices to moderate during 2027, particularly after the winter period with Brent oil prices approaching 80 USD/bbl next summer."
Oil and US yields could still pull the Euro lower
Standard Chartered's Steve Englander cautions against treating the Euro's difficulties as exclusively French.
His analysis links the recent decline to higher US yields relative to Germany, widening borrowing premiums within the Eurozone and rising oil prices, while acknowledging that their separate effects are difficult to isolate.
Those risks are related: stronger US growth can lift Treasury yields while increasing concern about Europe's capacity to cope with higher borrowing costs.
Englander writes: "Alternatively, if the driver of higher yields is higher oil prices, all three EUR negatives could be pushing in the same direction simultaneously, as has been the case over the last seven weeks."
"Even having two of three factors pushing in the same direction is likely to be enough to put some downward pressure on the EUR. So while the market may pause to absorb recent moves, we could easily see a resumption of EUR depreciation down the road."
EUR/USD Exchange Rate FAQ
What is UBS's EUR/USD exchange rate forecast?
UBS expects $1.16 by end-2026 and $1.20 by June 2027. Its recovery case includes lower energy prices and reduced French political uncertainty.
Does Crédit Agricole expect more ECB rate rises?
Yes. It forecasts quarter-point increases in December and March, taking the deposit rate to 3% in March 2027. That is an interest-rate projection, not an exchange-rate target.
Why might higher European rates fail to lift the Euro?
Some tightening is already priced in. Expensive energy and widening government borrowing premiums can also weaken growth and confidence in European assets.

articles.title: AI-driven demand has propelled emerging market earnings expectations higher, while the valuation discount relative to U.S. equities has reached a 20-year high. - Moomoo
articles.summary: AI-driven demand has propelled emerging market earnings expectations higher, while the valuation discount relative to U.S. equities has reached a 20-year high.  Moomoo
articles.full_text:
Earnings expectations for emerging markets have surged 70% year-to-date, driven by AI demand, while valuations have hit a record low, trading at a 47% discount to U.S. equities.
The Zhitong Finance app notes that earnings expectations for emerging-market stocks have continued to surge, pushing their valuations to historically low levels relative to their U.S. counterparts, potentially presenting a buying opportunity for long-term investors.
The MSCI Emerging Markets Index currently trades at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of just under 9x, based on projected earnings over the next 12 months, while the S&P 500's comparable valuation stands at around 19x. The valuation discount of emerging-market equities relative to U.S. stocks has widened to 53%, the highest level since Bloomberg began compiling this data in 2006.
So far this year, the emerging markets index has risen 15%, outpacing the S&P 500 by roughly 3 percentage points. Upgrades to earnings forecasts have been far more rapid than the rally in stock prices, thereby pushing valuations lower.
AI companies have accounted for the bulk of earnings upgrades in emerging markets. While U.S. hyperscale cloud providers are heavily investing in AI development, tech firms in developing economies are largely footing the bill, supplying chips, components, and hardware to support AI infrastructure.
Emerging-market stocks are becoming increasingly cheap.
This has prompted analysts to raise their earnings forecasts for emerging-market technology stocks, even as concerns about AI valuations are broadly prompting investors to pull out of the sector.
Mark Matthews, head of Asian research at Baosheng Media Group in Singapore, said: "The prices of products manufactured by Asian technology companies—namely semiconductors and related hardware—have not yet fallen." "U.S. technology companies have generally been raising their earnings forecasts for analysts. They are the largest customers of Asian semiconductor and related hardware firms."
The profit outlook is very promising.
The consensus 12-month forward earnings estimate for companies in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index has surged 70% this year alone, hitting record highs. Asia leads with an 87% upward revision to earnings per share, while Latin America contributes 28%; by contrast, Emerging Europe, the Middle East, and Africa—regions at the epicenter of multiple conflicts and debt crises—lag behind, with a modest 8.6% increase.
Led by the Asian market
The emerging markets information technology sub-index has risen 63% this year, compared with a 23% gain for the S&P 500 information technology index. Profit expectations for the emerging markets index have also been revised upward by 128%.
Despite capital flows and market dominance shifting away from AI stocks, tech companies continue to demonstrate strong earnings momentum. Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM.US) issued a better-than-expected earnings outlook, prompting analysts to further raise their forecasts. However, since the update, the stock has declined as investors have fled the overcrowded AI sector.
Robert Ness, a portfolio manager at Nordic Investment Management, said, "Clearly, concerns about the sustainability of AI‑related investments are growing." "However, what particularly strikes me is that earnings expectations remain exceptionally strong, even as stock prices have collapsed."

articles.full_text:
Gold prices fell again in early Asian trading on Tuesday as investors awaited the US Federal Reserve's upcoming interest rate decision and key inflation data.
Spot gold fell 0.3% to $4,126.84 an ounce at 7:02am Bangladesh time on Tuesday (October 20). US gold futures for December delivery also declined 0.3% to $4,146 an ounce.
Investors are focusing on the Federal Reserve's monetary policy meeting scheduled for October 27–28. They are also awaiting the US personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, due next week. The index is a key measure of inflation and plays an important role in the Fed's policy decisions. The central bank has an inflation target of 2%.
In September, the Fed raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to a range of 3.75%–4%. According to the CME FedWatch Tool, market participants see an 83% probability that the Fed will keep rates unchanged at its upcoming meeting. Meanwhile, the probability of a rate hike in December is estimated at 94%.
Higher interest rates generally put pressure on gold prices because the precious metal does not pay interest. As rates rise, the opportunity cost of holding gold increases, making interest-bearing assets relatively more attractive to investors.
Investors are also monitoring geopolitical developments. On Monday, Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen claimed to have carried out multiple attacks targeting energy facilities, airports and military sites in Saudi Arabia. Such developments can influence demand for safe-haven assets, including gold.
Among other precious metals, spot silver fell 0.7% to $56.69 an ounce. Platinum remained almost unchanged at $1,639.65 an ounce, while palladium declined 0.7% to $1,112.08 an ounce.

articles.title: Fed Rate Polymarket Odds: October Hold Could Ease Bitcoin Pressure - Bitget
articles.summary: Fed Rate Polymarket Odds: October Hold Could Ease Bitcoin Pressure  Bitget
articles.full_text:
Fed Rate Polymarket odds show an approximately 78% probability of no change at the Federal Reserve’s October 27–28 meeting, while New York Fed President John Williams said he still considers one more rate hike potentially appropriate in 2026 but currently sees no need for additional increases in 2027.
The prediction-market figure is a changeable snapshot, not a Federal Reserve decision or a signal that Williams has endorsed an October hold. This is not simply a repricing toward easier policy.
It is a near-term reprieve within a path that still allows another increase this year, with Bitcoin and other liquidity-sensitive assets exposed to changes in the expected timing of interest rates.
The distinction matters for Bitcoin’s sensitivity to October Fed expectations: a higher probability of a hold may ease immediate rate-path pressure, but it does not establish that tightening is over.
Fed Rate Polymarket Odds: A Hold Signal, Not a Policy Pivot
Williams’s position leaves the timing question open. He maintained that one additional 2026 increase may be appropriate, while saying he did not currently see a reason to expect further hikes in 2027. His assessment is not an explicit recommendation for the October meeting, and it does not rule out a move later in the year.
That qualification contrasts with other market measures. The Business Times reported on October 14 that investors, as reflected in federal funds futures pricing, anticipated a December increase and two more hikes in 2027. That futures-based outlook is separate from Polymarket’s event-contract odds; treat the two measures as distinct forecasts.
The market distinction matters for crypto because expectations about the pace and duration of restrictive policy can influence liquidity and risk appetite.
A softer near-term path could reduce one source of pressure on Bitcoin, Ethereum, and altcoins, but a December hike still leaves another risk in place. This remains conditional analysis, not evidence that crypto prices have already reacted to Polymarket’s odds.
Interest Rates: Inflation Data and Treasury Yields Remain Central
Away from the Fed rate Polymarket odds, the Federal Reserve raised rates by a quarter percentage point at its September meeting. Williams’s September 29 remarks about a lack of urgency after that move helped rein in expectations for another increase in October, the report said; he later emphasized that the speech reflected his own views.
Policymakers were due to receive a fresh consumer-price report before the October 27–28 meeting. That reading gives markets another inflation signal to weigh against Williams’s view that price growth could slow and approach the Fed’s 2% target in 2027 as tariff and energy-price effects fade.
Williams also pointed to uncertainty around inflation tied to artificial-intelligence infrastructure: demand in that part of the economy was outpacing supply, though he continued to monitor whether the pressure would affect the broader outlook. The Business Times reported that two-year Treasury yields, which are particularly sensitive to expectations for the Fed’s rate path, erased an increase of as much as three basis points after his remarks.
The analytical question is no longer whether an October hold is possible; Polymarket’s snapshot puts that outcome well ahead of a hike. It is whether incoming inflation data and Treasury yields keep that expectation intact while leaving room for a 2026 hike. Changing central-bank rate expectations and Bitcoin volatility are linked through that repricing channel, but Williams’s comments do not settle the policy path.

articles.title: Are we there yet? Bull market may have more miles - Invesco
articles.summary: Are we there yet? Bull market may have more miles  Invesco
articles.full_text:
Markets and Economy Are we there yet? Bull market may have more miles
Key takeaways
- Some credit markets became more selective, but stress hasn't broadened to all areas of the credit markets. Companies with stronger balance sheets and cash flows may continue to access capital.
- Recent inflation data has been uncomfortably strong, but longer-term inflation expectations have remained relatively contained, and concerns about confidence in US assets may be limited.
- The indicators we watch have suggested that the ride may be slowing, but that the bull market doesn’t appear to be coming to an end, and may not be for a while.
We recently drove our oldest daughter to college. Ten hours in the car gives you plenty of time to think. At some point, I remembered the question I used to ask my parents on long road trips.
“Are we there yet?”
“No.”
“When will we be there?”
“Not for a while.”
“Are we getting closer?”
“Well, of course we are.”
That exchange feels surprisingly relevant for investors today.
It has been a long, positive ride for the US stock market.1 History offers some warning signs on how things have tended to end. Too much borrowing. Too much inflation. Too much monetary policy tightening. Credit spreads widen. Investors paying up for default protection. Cyclical stocks selling off. Treasury yields falling as investors seek safety. The US dollar strengthening.
That’s a reasonable recap of the news flow over the past few weeks,2 but it doesn’t necessarily mean that the bull market ride is ending.
Credit stress has risen, but not broadened
Start with leverage. The rapid buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure has increasingly depended on debt financing, and the bond market has started distinguishing among borrowers.3 CoreWeave is the latest example. Yields on some of its unsecured debt have climbed to roughly 15%, while the cost of insuring its debt against default has risen sharply.4 Since June, wider credit spreads have accounted for roughly half of the increase in high-yield borrowing costs.5 The rise may no longer simply be a rates story. It increasingly appears to reflect concerns about credit quality.
That shouldn’t be dismissed. But neither should it automatically be interpreted as the end of the AI investment cycle, in my view. Demand for computing capacity has remained substantial. I believe the more likely consequence may be that capital becomes more discriminating. Companies with stronger balance sheets, visible cash flows, contractual support, and better financing structures will likely continue to have access to capital, in my opinion. Weaker, more leveraged projects may find that capital becomes prohibitively expensive or unavailable. Importantly, spreads in the higher quality parts of the bond market remained relatively tight, suggesting that the stresses haven’t broadened across credit markets.6 That’s what credit markets are supposed to do. They differentiate.
Leverage is one thing. Leverage combined with Federal Reserve (Fed) tightening is another. As rates rise, financing has gotten more expensive, and the economy has tended to slow. That doesn’t mean the journey is ending, but it may be a sign that we’re getting closer.
Markets appear prepared for tighter policy
That brings us to inflation. Recent inflation data have been uncomfortably strong.7 But the bond market rallied in response to the strong Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index releases.8 That suggests to me that markets had already priced in the rate hikes and are now preparing for tighter policy to slow economic activity. Importantly, longer-term inflation expectations have remained relatively contained.9 The recent rally in US Treasuries and resilience of the US dollar10 suggests to me concerns about confidence in US assets may be limited. That seems like a signal that the recent rise in yields may never have been primarily about concerns over fiscal sustainability.
Journey continues, quality matters
None of this means investors should ignore what’s happening. Cycles generally haven’t ended without warning. Financing became more expensive. Credit became more selective. Weakness appeared in the more speculative corners of the market.
Those mile markers matter.
That also has implications for how we invest. As the credit markets become more discerning and the economy slows, we favor higher-quality credit and more defensive sectors of the stock market. We also watch for signs of a reacceleration in economic activity, which could occur with a resolution of the oil shocks, and/or a rally in bond prices.
So, are we there yet?
No, I don’t think so.
Are we getting closer?
Sure. Every mile of a long journey gets you closer to the destination.
The indicators we watch suggest the ride may have slowed, but I don’t believe the bull market is over yet, and it may not be for a while.

articles.title: Nearly $1 million worth of rare Pokemon and sports cards stolen from FedEx truck in Orange County heist, police say - ABC7 Los Angeles
articles.summary: Nearly $1 million worth of rare Pokemon and sports cards stolen from FedEx truck in Orange County heist, police say  ABC7 Los AngelesAt least $963,000 in trading cards stolen from FedEx truck in California  ESPNPokémon and Sports Cards Worth Nearly $1 Million Stolen from FedEx Truck, Police Say Value Could Be Higher  People.comThieves steal nearly $1 million worth of Pokémon cards in SoCal FedEx truck break in  ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Vid...
articles.full_text:
SANTA ANA, Calif. (KABC) -- Nearly $1 million in rare trading cards, including highly valued Pokémon cards, were stolen from a FedEx truck parked near an Orange County business that authenticates and grades the collectible items, according to police.
The theft is the latest in a string of heists involving Pokémon cards, which have exponentially increased in value in recent years.
The Santa Ana Police Department said in a statement on Tuesday that the heist occurred on Oct. 13 outside the Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA) office in Santa Ana.
The hundreds of stolen cards are estimated to be worth a total of $963,000, according to police.
"However, the exact value of the stolen items has not yet been determined," according to the Santa Ana police statement.
The cards belong to collectors from across the country who submitted them to the PSA to be authenticated and graded.
Two full pallets of collectible cards were stolen, and some cards on a third pallet were also swiped when thieves broke into a FedEx truck, according to police.
"The pallets contained various trading cards, including, but not limited to, sports cards and Pokémon cards," according to the police statement.
As of Tuesday, no arrests have been announced in the memorabilia rip-off. Police said the investigation is ongoing.
The theft was first reported by The Athletic, which cited police sources saying the the FedEx truck was broken into during the 60 to 90 minutes the driver was away from the parked vehicle.
"We are aware of a theft involving a third-party shipping vehicle carrying PSA-graded items. We are working closely with law enforcement and the carrier as the investigation continues," Collectors, the parent company of PSA, said in a statement to ABC News.
The company said it deactivated the certificates for the missing cards and has notified its "marketplace partners to be on the lookout for rare and serialized items."
"Our customer service team has contacted affected customers directly and is arranging compensation based on fair market value," the company said. "We understand the impact this has on collectors involved, many of whom see these cards as far more than a financial asset."
FedEx released a statement to ABC7, saying, "The security of our customers' shipments is a top priority, and we are working with local law enforcement in their investigation. Further questions should be referred to local investigators."
One victimized collector, known by his online handle, Sky-B Cards, issued a YouTube video statement, saying the 104 cards he submitted to PSA for grading were among the stolen items. He said he paid more than $8,000 to have the cards graded by PSA and that his cards were insured for more than $150,000.
"These were 104 cards that I've accumulated over two years," Sky-B Cards said in the YouTube video. "There are many irreplaceable cards in here that I will never see again, and honestly that's what hurts the most, outside of being absolutely financially destroyed here."
The heist is the latest in a string of thefts in Southern California and elsewhere in the country of highly valued Pokémon cards, highlighting what appears to be an ever-growing demand for merchandise from the popular childhood card game.
In February, thieves broke into a collectibles shop in Anaheim, by cutting a hole through the wall from a neighboring shop they also broke into, stealing tens of thousands of dollars worth of Pokémon cards.
Captured on video surveillance cameras, the three thieves were seen grabbing hundreds of trading cards and bolting from the shop in less than 10 minutes.
In April, thieves staged a smash-and-grab heist at Elite Sports Cards in Chicago, stealing $100,000 in Pokémon cards, the store owner told ABC Chicago station WLS.
In an interview in April, Jared Mast, president of Mast Wealth Management Group, which deals in alternative investments including collectibles like Pokémon cards, told ABC News the value of Pokémon cards has risen sharply in the past year.
"I would say, collectively, over the last 12 months, things have gone up anywhere from 200 to 300%," Mast said.
Mast explained that Pokémon card value has risen in three different waves over the last decade. First, in 2016, with the arrival of Pokémon Go, the popular mobile game based on the playing cards, and then again in 2019 and 2020, as a generation of celebrities like Logan Paul invested in the collectibles.
ABC News contributed to this report.

articles.title: Global oil prices hit highest level in 5 months amid attacks on ships, facilities - ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.summary: Global oil prices hit highest level in 5 months amid attacks on ships, facilities  ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and VideosOil rises on Middle East supply worries  CNBCBrent crude edges lower, even after Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure  ReutersOil parked above $110 a barrel as IEA warns energy markets won’t return to normal next year  CNNBrent falls as Iran's president discusses mediation with Pakistani army chief  Yahoo Finance

source_detail.name: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos

articles.full_text:
Global oil prices have climbed more than 55% since the outbreak of the Iran war.
Global oil prices climbed to their highest level in five months on Tuesday after Iran and its Houthi allies claimed attacks on oil infrastructure in the Middle East.
The Brent crude futures price, a benchmark for global trading, topped $111 a barrel for the first time since May before retreating to $110.30 a barrel. The latest reading marks a rise of more than 55% since the Iran war began in late February.
An oil shortage continues to bedevil crude sellers, who typically pass along elevated costs to refiners, leading to higher prices at the pump.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Center, or UKMTO, on Tuesday issued an advisory after it received a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces off the coast of Oman.
Separately, Iranian state-run media reported on Tuesday that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed that two oil tankers hit naval mines south of the Strait of Hormuz.
The reports came a day after Yemen-based Houthi militants claimed a wave of strikes on Saudia Arabia on Monday, including the Shaybah oil field as well as Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu, a port city near a key transport corridor on the Red Sea.
The West Texas Intermediate futures price, a benchmark index for U.S. trading, also jumped on Tuesday. The price of U.S. oil prices stands at $105.75, a rise of more than 60% since the outbreak of the war.
The jump in oil prices arrived as affordability marks a top concern for voters ahead of early November's midterm elections.
The average price of a gallon of gas in the U.S. clocked in at $4.27 on Tuesday, according to AAA. That figure amounts to a rise of nearly $1.30 since the start late February.
The Middle East conflict drove up fuel prices and catapulted U.S. inflation to a three-year high in May, but inflation eased slightly over the summer after a preliminary peace agreement established an on-again, off-again pause in fighting.
The tentative accord between the U.S. and Iran expired in August, giving way to continued attacks on oil infrastructure and ships in the region.
The U.S. -- the world's largest oil producer -- imports a small amount of crude from the Middle East. Since oil and gas are sold on a global market, however, the shortage has sent prices rising for everyone, including U.S. drivers.
ABC News' Nasser Atta, Othon Leyva and Desiree Adib contributed to this report.

articles.title: GM beats on Q3 results, tightens profit outlook, unveils new $20 billion buyback - Yahoo Finance
articles.summary: GM beats on Q3 results, tightens profit outlook, unveils new $20 billion buyback  Yahoo FinanceGM shares sink as automaker signals rising cost pressures  ReutersGeneral Motors beats Wall Street's Q3 earnings expectations, narrows full-year guidance  CNBCGM Plans $20 Billion in Buybacks, but Warns of Bumpy 2027  WSJGM Slides as CEO Barra Warns of ‘Intensifying’ Challenges  Bloomberg.com
articles.full_text:
GM (GM) posted third quarter results before the bell that topped estimates, tightened its full-year profit outlook instead of boosting it, but issued shareholders a new $20 billion share repurchase program instead.
For the quarter, GM posted Q3 revenue of $50.0 billion, up 2.9% from a year ago and above the $48.52 billion Bloomberg consensus. GM posted adjusted EPS of $3.70 versus $3.57 estimated, with adjusted EBIT coming in at $4.1 billion, ahead of the $4.02 billion expected and up nearly 22%.
But the big update was guidance. For the full year, GM now expects:
- Adjusted EBIT of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion (prior $14 billion to $16 billion)
- Adjusted EPS of $12.75 to $13.75 (prior $12 to $14)
- Adjusted automotive free cash flow of $11.5 billion to $12.5 billion (prior $9.5 billion to $11.5 billion)
Investors were hoping for more, as the stock is getting hit in early trading, down over 5%.
Both ranges keep the same midpoints as before — $15 billion and $13.25 billion — meaning GM trimmed the upside as much as the downside.
GM also lifted its adjusted automotive free cash flow forecast to $11.5 billion to $12.5 billion from $9.5 billion to $11.5 billion.
GM's board approved a new $20 billion multiyear authorization with no expiration date. GM also declared a quarterly dividend of $0.18 per share.
"We think this is a proven strategy," GM CEO Mary Barra wrote in her letter to shareholders. "The new $20 billion multiyear share repurchase authorization we announced today further demonstrates our board's commitment to creating even greater shareholder value."
Barra also said GM is working to continue its momentum "despite growing inflationary pressures."
This is seen with GM's costs creeping up. GM now expects commodity inflation of about $2 billion (the top of its prior $1.5 billion-$2 billion range), including logistics and memory chip (DRAM) costs. It also cut its expected regulatory benefits to about $500 million from as much as $750 million. Offsetting that, gross tariff costs are tracking toward the low end of its $2.5 billion-$3.5 billion range.
Earlier this month, GM reported third quarter US sales of 670,974 vehicles, a drop of 5.5% compared to a year ago, as a collapse in EV sales offset gains from its pickups and small SUVs.
Based on GM's model-by-model figures, EV sales fell about 62% to roughly 25.5K units, shrinking to under 4% of GM's US volume from more than 9% a year ago. Excluding EVs, GM's sales were essentially flat, up 0.3%.
Sales of the Chevrolet Equinox EV plunged 92.4% to 1,905, the Blazer EV dropped 84.4%, the GMC Hummer EV slid 72.9%, and the Cadillac Lyriq fell 50.5%.

articles.title: [SMM Iron Ore] Imported iron ore margins narrow to 9.62 yuan/mt on higher brand premiums - Shanghai Metals Market
articles.summary: [SMM Iron Ore] Imported iron ore margins narrow to 9.62 yuan/mt on higher brand premiums  Shanghai Metals Market
articles.full_text:
The average margin on imported iron ore narrowed to 9.62 yuan/mt today from 11.52 yuan/mt, driven mainly by higher premiums on some brands alongside weaker spot prices.
On the supply side, BHP’s Q1 FY2027 report showed Western Australia Iron Ore (WAIO) production at 71.91 million mt on a 100% basis, up 2.4% year-on-year, with full-year guidance unchanged at 286-298 million mt. Lump accounted for 27.9% of WAIO sales, the lowest in five quarters. Mainstream supply volumes were steady and the loose supply-side picture was unchanged. On freight, SMM data showed the Australia-China route up 0.49/mt week-on-week at 11.91/mt on 19 October, while the Brazil-China route eased to 30.46/mt. The net change in CFR costs was limited.
On the demand side, mills remain lossmaking and restocking is still on a just-in-need basis, with port inventories building again last week. Futures lost upward momentum after yesterday’s rebound and spot prices edged lower. Iron ore prices are likely to stay range-bound in the near term with limited upside, and import margins are expected to hold in modest positive territory.

The US dollar and the euro rose again this Tuesday, October 20, in the informal currency market in Cuba, reaching 818 and 908 Cuban pesos (CUP), respectively, according to the reference values of as of 8:00 p.m. local time.
Both currencies continue their upward trend and reach their highest values in the last 30 days, while the Convertible Currency (MLC) experiences a slight decline, though limited data necessitates a cautious interpretation of its quotation.
The dollar closed this Tuesday at 818 CUP, five pesos above the 813 recorded on the previous day.
In the past seven days, the U.S. dollar has recorded an increase of 25 pesos, rising from 793 CUP from a week ago, which is equivalent to a rise of 3.2%.
The euro gains three pesos and closes at 908 CUP
The euro reaches 908 CUP, an increase of three pesos compared to Monday, when it was priced at 905 CUP.
Exchange Rate Evolution
The European currency has accumulated an increase of 20 pesos over the past week, equivalent to 2.3%, and remains the most expensive currency among the main references of the informal market, with a difference of 90 pesos compared to the dollar.
The MLC is around 587 CUP, six pesos less than the 593 recorded on Monday.
Despite this setback, it has accumulated an increase of 37 pesos in the last seven days. Its quotation continues to be influenced by the scarcity of available data, so it should be regarded as indicative.

articles.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Hits 5.15%, Tightening the Squeeze on Borrowers - 24/7 Wall St.
articles.summary: 10-Year Treasury Yield Hits 5.15%, Tightening the Squeeze on Borrowers  24/7 Wall St.
articles.full_text:
As seen on the 24/7 Wall St. homepage on October 21, 2026.
The benchmark yield is back above 5% and holding there, which keeps mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs and every rate-sensitive stock under pressure. Savers weighing whether to lock in have a narrowing window if the Fed hikes again in December.
Source: FRED · DGS10
Continue ReadingShow less
The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.15%, holding the benchmark rate well above the 5% level after spending much of the year in the mid-4% range.
For mortgage borrowers, the connection is direct. The 10-year yield serves as the primary benchmark lenders use to price home loans, so a rate held above 5% keeps monthly financing costs elevated and continues to weigh on housing affordability.
Corporate borrowers feel the same drag. When the risk-free rate sits at 5.15%, companies issuing new debt must offer higher coupons to attract buyers, raising the cost of refinancing existing obligations and putting new investment plans under greater scrutiny. Rate-sensitive sectors, including utilities, real estate investment trusts, and high-growth equities, tend to reprice lower as the discount rate applied to their future earnings rises.
The Federal Reserve's next meeting sharpens the stakes: another move before year-end adds upward pressure on yields, narrowing the window for borrowers and investors waiting for rates to pull back before acting.

articles.title: PBoC is expected to set USD/CNY mid-point at 6.6779 (Prev. 6.7200) - Newsquawk
articles.summary: PBoC is expected to set USD/CNY mid-point at 6.6779 (Prev. 6.7200)  Newsquawk
articles.full_text:
What it means
The expected mid-point implies a firmer yuan fix than the prior session, and with the onshore spot confined to its daily band around the fix, the setting is the PBoC's primary steering instrument rather than a passive reference rate. In past episodes of sustained yuan strength, the operative question has been whether the fixing merely tracks overnight dollar moves or deliberately leans into appreciation, a distinction usually read from the gap between the actual fix and model-derived consensus, since a materially stronger fix than models imply signals intent rather than mechanics. Periods where the fix has consistently printed on the strong side of estimates have historically coincided with efforts to attract inflows, steady sentiment around trade negotiations, or rebuild policy credibility, while the reverse has flagged tolerance for depreciation. The accompanying tells are the onshore-offshore spread, since a CNH premium to CNY points to offshore scepticism about the move's durability, and any visible state bank activity in the spot market around the open. Worth noting is that a stronger fix tightens the ceiling on USD/CNY for the session mechanically, so follow-through depends on where spot opens relative to the band rather than on the fix alone. As a daily operational signal, single fixings are noise; it is the run of consecutive strong-side surprises that has historically carried information about policy stance.

articles.title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6779 – Reuters estimate - investingLive
articles.summary: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6779 – Reuters estimate  investingLive
articles.full_text:
Summary
- PBOC CNY reference rate setting for the trading session ahead.
The fixing mechanism matters most right now because its message has shifted over the past month. For nearly a year, the PBOC has set its daily guidance weaker than market expectations, which traders read as an effort to slow the yuan's appreciation, and in late August that gap reached its widest since February, shortly after the yuan touched a three-and-a-half-year high. Through October, however, the midpoint has strengthened at a faster pace, narrowing its gap with market expectations and suggesting the central bank has eased its resistance to yuan gains. The fixing is still set weaker than models imply, so this looks like a loosening of the brakes rather than their removal. The balance Beijing is weighing is unchanged: a firmer currency supports capital stability and import costs, but too rapid a rise risks eroding export competitiveness while the domestic economy remains soft. The gap between each day's fixing and consensus estimates remains one of the clearest guides to how far the PBOC is willing to let the yuan run.
---
The daily fixing is Beijing's quietest but clearest tool for telling markets how fast it wants the yuan to move, and after months of saying slow down, it has lately been saying go, gradually.
Summary:
- The PBOC sets the daily USD/CNY reference rate, or midpoint, at around 0115 GMT, one of the most closely watched signals in Asian FX markets.
- China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, allowing the yuan to trade within a band of plus or minus 2% around the daily midpoint during onshore hours.
- The midpoint reflects a mix of inputs, including the prior day's close, moves in major currencies, broader international FX conditions and domestic factors such as capital flows and growth momentum, with policymakers retaining discretion over the final number.
- If market pressure pushes the yuan toward either edge of the band, the PBOC can intervene through direct buying or selling of yuan, liquidity adjustments, or guidance via state-owned banks.
- A stronger-than-expected fixing typically signals the PBOC is leaning against depreciation, while a weaker fixing can indicate tolerance for a softer currency or discomfort with the pace of gains.
- For nearly a year the fixing has been set weaker than market estimates, with the gap reaching its widest since February in late August.
- In October the midpoint reached its strongest level since February 2023.
- The yuan has pushed to its strongest levels since early 2023 onshore and since mid-2022 offshore
The People's Bank of China sets the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT, a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. It has taken on added significance in recent weeks as policymakers have shifted from restraining the yuan's rise to guiding it higher.
China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the yuan is allowed to trade within a band of plus or minus 2% around the central midpoint set each trading day. That midpoint reflects a mix of inputs, including the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies such as the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic considerations like capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The calculation is not purely mechanical, giving policymakers room to use the fixing to guide market expectations.
Once the midpoint is set, onshore USD/CNY trades freely within the allowable range. Should market pressure push the currency toward either edge of that band, the central bank can step in to smooth volatility, whether through direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance channelled through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often read as a policy signal rather than a purely technical reference point. A stronger-than-expected midpoint typically suggests the PBOC is leaning against depreciation, while a weaker fixing can signal tolerance for a softer currency, or unease with how quickly the yuan is rising.
That second reading has dominated for much of the past year. For nearly a year, the central bank set its daily guidance weaker than market expectations, a pattern traders and analysts interpreted as an attempt to slow the yuan's appreciation. The gap reached its widest since February in late August, shortly after the yuan touched a three-and-a-half-year high against the dollar.
September has brought a clear change of tone. The midpoint has strengthened at a faster pace this month, narrowing its gap with market expectations and suggesting the PBOC has eased its resistance to yuan gains. The central bank strengthened the fixing for eight consecutive sessions, the longest streak since 2023, and the midpoint has since reached its strongest level since February 2023. The onshore yuan has traded at its strongest since January 2023, while the offshore rate has reached levels last seen in July 2022. Even so, the fixing is still being set well weaker than market estimates, with one recent midpoint more than 500 pips below a Reuters survey forecast, a reminder that Beijing is allowing appreciation on its own terms rather than stepping aside.
The timing has been linked to diplomacy.
The underlying tension is a familiar one. A firmer yuan supports capital stability and eases import costs, but a rapid rise risks undermining export competitiveness at a moment when China's broader economy continues to show signs of softness. For traders and investors, the gap between each day's fixing and consensus estimates remains one of the clearest windows into how Beijing is weighing that trade-off, and whether the recent green light for gains stays in place once the summit has passed.

articles.title: FAA clears the way for airlines to put Boeing’s long-delayed 737 Max 10 into service - AP News
articles.summary: FAA clears the way for airlines to put Boeing’s long-delayed 737 Max 10 into service  AP NewsBoeing’s Large 737 Max Jet Secures U.S. Approval  The New York TimesBoeing wins FAA approval for 737 Max 10 after years of delays as Duffy says certification process should be faster  CNBCU.S. FAA certifies Boeing 737-10, largest member of 737 MAX family  Boeing NewsroomUS set to announce certification of Boeing 737 MAX 10 on Tuesday, sources say  Reuters
articles.full_text:
Nearly a decade after Boeing unveiled its largest 737 Max jet, the company has cleared a major hurdle in its effort to bring the plane to airlines. The Federal Aviation Administration approved the Max 10 for passenger service Tuesday, ending years of delays.
The 737 Max 10’s certification represents another milestone in Boeing’s efforts to restore its reputation and financial footing after years of safety, quality and production challenges. With production approved, the aircraft can now be sold to domestic and foreign carriers.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the certification followed “extensive safety reviews,” including thousands of hours of test flights, and called it a major win for American manufacturing.
“To think that it took us almost 10 years to get here. We all probably had a little less gray hair 10 years ago,” Duffy said during a visit to Boeing’s manufacturing plant Tuesday in Everett, Washington.
The Max 10 is an important piece of the company’s effort to regain ground in the narrow-body market. For airlines, the larger plane offers a way to carry more passengers on a single flight, potentially lowering costs per seat. For travelers, it could eventually mean more seats on popular routes, though the impact on fares will depend on how airlines deploy the planes and how much competition they face.
Stephanie Pope, president and CEO of Boeing Commercial Airplanes, said during Duffy’s visit that the certification “clears the path to deliver an airplane that will set a new standard in commercial aviation.” The Max 10 will typically seat 185-210 passengers, according to Boeing, compared with 175-195 on the Max 9 and 160-180 on the Max 8.
“Today is a very, very special day. It caps years of hard work and dedication by many,” Pope said. “It marks another major milestone in our recovery, and it unlocks a key to our future growth.”
The company expects to begin deliveries in 2027.
The single-aisle jet was introduced at the Paris air show in 2017 to help Boeing compete with rival Airbus. But technical and regulatory hurdles repeatedly delayed certification.
Boeing’s struggles have been particularly acute since two deadly crashes involving the smaller Max 8 killed 346 people in 2018 and 2019 off the coast of Indonesia and in Ethiopia. In 2024, a panel flew off of an Alaska Airlines Max 9 in midair, renewing scrutiny of Boeing’s manufacturing and safety practices.
The delays have held up a key part of Boeing’s business. More than 30 customers worldwide have ordered 1,555 Max 10s that Boeing has yet to deliver, accounting for more than 30% of its total 737 Max backlog.
Major customers include United Airlines, Delta Air Lines, American Airlines and Ryanair. Alaska Airlines joined that list in January, ordering 105 Max 10s, with options for 35 more.
The Max 10 is intended to compete with Airbus’s A321neo model family, which entered service in 2017. The largest A321neo can carry more passengers and fly farther without refueling than the Max 10.
Still, Boeing designed the Max 10 to carry more passengers while burning less fuel than older aircraft — a potentially attractive combination for airlines facing soaring jet fuel costs amid the U.S. war with Iran. Those rising costs have put added pressure on airlines to control expenses.
Certification means the FAA has determined that the Max 10’s design meets safety standards, following engineering reviews and flight testing. But Boeing must continue to show it can consistently build the aircraft to the approved design, and each plane must be cleared before it can fly passengers.
The Max 10’s certification completes the lineup of four 737 Max models. The FAA cleared the Max 7 for airline operations in August.
Pope on Tuesday described the certification of both the Max 7 and Max 10 in the same year as a sign of the company’s resilience.
In the wake of the fatal Max 8 crashes, the FAA overhauled how it certifies Boeing aircraft. But over the past 18 months, the agency has gradually eased some of its restrictions on the company, increasing the limit on how many planes Boeing can produce. In July, the FAA also said Boeing could once again issue airworthiness certificates for its 737 Max and 787 planes at the end of production, allowing the company to take back some responsibility for determining whether finished aircraft are ready to fly.
